evaluator: Prof. Margaret Morse lens source audit
evidence: The About page named civic technology, cultural infrastructure, coalition work, and collective credit.
WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, and NYC Artist Coalition pages separately documented participation, care, and cultural-space practice.
gaps: No public surface connected the artistic, civic, technical, and social practices as one lineage.
The dominant frame was organizational utility: workflows, interfaces, coordination, and handoffs.
Experimentation, attention, place, hospitality, embodiment, and how people inhabit systems were not legible as causes of the operating method.
safety_findings: Collective-credit and privacy language was strong.
No protected UCSC educational record or private testimonial appeared on the public site.
recommendation: Add one concise, public-source-backed threshold connecting the participatory artistic lineage to current operating practice, while keeping private praise and participant details out.
